The All Progressives Congress (APC) has renewed efforts to reconcile Benue State Governor Hyacinth Alia and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, amid a prolonged leadership crisis that has divided the party in the state.
Mr Alia disclosed this in a post on his verified Facebook page on Sunday, saying he had attended a reconciliation meeting in Abuja convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee.
The committee is chaired by former Katsina State Governor Ibrahim Shema.
The meeting, which lasted about two hours, was attended by Mr Akume, former Benue Governor Gabriel Suswam, Senators Barnabas Gemade, Jack Gyado, and Simon Shango, among other stakeholders.
Mr Alia thanked Mr Shema and members of the committee for bringing the leaders together, saying reconciliation required a willingness to listen, speak frankly and continue working together despite differences.
“I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain,” he said.
The governor said he would continue engaging with party leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while prioritising peace, security and development in Benue.

He added that the responsibility the people entrusted to political leaders should guide their actions.
Mr Alia did not disclose the specific issues discussed at the meeting or whether the participants had reached any agreement to resolve the crisis.
The meeting comes amid a prolonged disagreement between factions of the Benue APC loyal to Mr Alia and Mr Akume, centred on control of the party’s structures and influence over its political affairs.
The dispute has produced parallel party executives and competing claims over the leadership of the state chapter.
On 4 March, the two camps held separate state congresses in Makurdi. Mr Alia’s faction returned Benjamin Omale as state chairman, while the Akume-aligned faction affirmed the Austin Agada-led executive committee for another four-year term.
The factions have also disagreed over political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
PREMIUM TIMES reported on 15 November that the Director-General of the Tinubu-Alia 2027 Campaign Council, Richard Asema, accused Mr Akume, Minister of Water Resources, Joseph Utsev, and other APC figures of working with opposition politicians through the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu-Shettima 2027.
The alliance’s Director-General, Akange Audu, rejected the allegation, describing it as political blackmail.
He said the group was an independent platform for mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and argued that supporting the president should not be made conditional on supporting Mr Alia.
PREMIUM TIMES also reported on 16 November that Mr Alia attributed the APC crisis to his refusal to share state funds with some party chieftains whom he accused of wanting to turn Benue into their private estate.
The governor, who made the allegation at the Adamawa State Tiv Day celebration in Yola, did not name the party leaders or provide details of the alleged demand.
The latest meeting represents another attempt to bridge the divisions among the party’s leading figures.
However, Mr Alia’s account did not indicate whether the reconciliation committee had secured any commitment from the rival camps or agreed on a framework for resolving their differences.
